question: Should OpenClaw adopt an immutable per-child-session `sessions_spawn.tools` capability policy, including fail-closed persisted-data handling and rejection of unsupported CLI/ACP policy shapes, as the supported core contract?
rationale: The patch is more than a local implementation detail: it defines durable authorization behavior stored in session state and changes the supported security boundary for all native subagents.

options.title: Approve the session policy contract
options.body: Accept the immutable persisted policy design, then require a rebased branch and real native-subagent proof before merge.

options.title: Narrow the feature first
options.body: Limit the first release to an allow-only or embedded-only contract if maintainers do not want deny semantics and runtime-specific failures in the initial API.

options.title: Keep the product item open
options.body: Pause this implementation if the repository does not yet want a core per-spawn capability API.

recommendation.title: Approve the session policy contract
recommendation.body: Accept the immutable persisted policy design, then require a rebased branch and real native-subagent proof before merge.
